title: Hardcoded SharePoint site URL in uploadToSharePoint — breaks on non-Prod environments
detail: Line 348: `return 'https://decadesconstructiongroup.sharepoint.com/sites/DCFGContractingSuite' + raw;` — the SharePoint site URL is hardcoded. If MsaComposer runs on Test or Stage (different org URLs), the constructed SharePoint link would still point to the Prod SharePoint site. Should read the base URL from dcfg_configs (the config table loaded at boot) or derive it from the document request response.
recommendedFix: Read the SharePoint base URL from getEnvVar('dcfg_sp_site_url') or similar config key. If the config value is not yet in dcfg_configs, add it. Alternatively, require the flow to always return a full URL (not a relative path) in dcfg_output_file_url.

title: Pricing configs apiGet uses raw entity set name instead of EntitySets constant, and missing $select
detail: Line 128: `apiGet('/dcfg_pricing_configs?$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true&$orderby=createdon desc')` — two issues: (1) uses hardcoded '/dcfg_pricing_configs' instead of EntitySets.pricingConfigs (no such constant exists in portalApi.js), breaking the single-source EntitySets pattern; (2) no $select clause, returning all columns which violates the 8a ($select safety) rule and may expose columns that aren't needed.
recommendedFix: Add `pricingConfigs: 'dcfg_pricing_configs'` to EntitySets in portalApi.js. Change to `apiGet('/${EntitySets.pricingConfigs}?$filter=...&$select=dcfg_pricing_configid,dcfg_name,...&$orderby=createdon desc')` with only the columns actually consumed.

title: MsaComposer does not import useMemo or useCallback — derived values recompute on every render
detail: Line 16: `import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';` — no useMemo or useCallback. The derived values (rate, obRate, billable, noc, moTotal, obTotal, annualMembership, totalContractValue, etc.) at lines 84-104 are recalculated on every render cycle including unrelated state changes. With a large location list these calculations could become noticeable. The sub-components (PackagePicker, CustomerSection, PricingSection, LocationsSection, FeeSummary, SignerForm) are all defined as standalone functions but receive new object/function references on every render because their props are not memoized.
evidence: Lines 84-104: const rate = loc => { ... }; const obRate = loc => { ... }; const billable = locs.filter(...); const moTotal = locs.reduce(...);
recommendedFix: Import useMemo and wrap the expensive derived values: const moTotal = useMemo(() => locs.reduce(...), [locs, priceMode, uniRate, typeRates]). For sub-components, consider React.memo wrapping or at least useMemo for the props objects. Low priority — unlikely to cause visible lag until location count > ~200.

title: Signer form inputs have labels but no htmlFor/id association
detail: Lines 582-590: SignerForm renders <label style={labelStyle}>Signer name</label> followed by <input>. The label has no htmlFor and the input has no id, so clicking the label text does not focus the input. Same for 'Signer title'. For accessibility, labels must be programmatically associated with their inputs.
recommendedFix: Add id="msa-signer-name" to the input and htmlFor="msa-signer-name" to the label. Same for title: id="msa-signer-title".

title: MSA date and MSA name inputs have labels without htmlFor/id association
detail: Lines 567-572: the 'MSA date' and 'MSA name (optional override)' labels have no htmlFor, and their corresponding inputs have no id. Same association gap as the signer form. Affects all labels in the CustomerSection sub-component (line 559 'Customer name' label also missing association).
recommendedFix: Add id/htmlFor pairs: msa-date, msa-name-override, msa-new-customer-name.

title: SharePoint upload polling has no user-visible progress beyond status text
detail: Lines 340-356: the upload polling loop runs for up to 90 seconds (18 iterations x 5s), during which the only visible indicator is the downloadStatus text 'Uploading to SharePoint...'. If the poll takes the full 90 seconds, the user stares at 'Uploading to SharePoint...' with no progress indicator. The Generate MSA button is disabled (downloading=true) but the user may think the app has frozen.
evidence: setDownloadStatus('Uploading to SharePoint...'); const maxAttempts = 18; for (let i = 0; i < maxAttempts; i++) { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5000)); ... }
recommendedFix: Update the downloadStatus text during each poll iteration: e.g., `setDownloadStatus('Uploading to SharePoint... (' + (i+1) + '/' + maxAttempts + ')')`. Or add an animated spinner next to the status text.

title: Service fee input has no label association
detail: Line 615: the 'Service fee %' input in the uniform pricing section has a <label> element but no htmlFor/id pairing, same as the other pricing inputs (uni-rate, uni-onboard). Those two have data-testids but still lack label association.
evidence: <label style={labelStyle}>Service fee %</label><input type="number" step="0.01" style={inputStyle} value={serviceFee} ... />
recommendedFix: Add id="msa-service-fee" and htmlFor="msa-service-fee". For uni-rate and uni-onboard, add htmlFor pointing to their existing inputs.
